$$\operatorname{Var}^{(n)}_{\mathrm{mat}}(E)=\frac{4n\bigl[(1+(n-1)p)D_n-n\bigr]}{D_n^2};\qquad n=3:\quad\frac{12\,p(1-p)(3-2p)}{D^2}\qquad[\mathrm{BM.94}(6)\ \textbf{reproduced exactly};\ \text{machine}];$$
$$n=1:\quad w_{\mathrm{mat}}^{(1)}=1:\qquad\textbf{a single materialized pair has no flicker: the restriction}\ E\ge2\ \textbf{forces its crystallized member}\qquad[\text{machine}];$$
$$(2)\quad\textbf{the two-chain ensemble measure (constructed):}\qquad\text{the meson floor}\ E^{cryst}=2E_{\mathrm{int}}(c)=4\ \ \text{is two pairs}\qquad[\mathrm{BM.111}(1);\ \text{the digon floor}\ E_{\mathrm{int}}(c)=2\ [\mathrm{FT.28};\ \mathrm{BM.13}(3)]]:$$
$$\boxed{\ P_{\mathrm{mat}}(E{=}2)=\frac{2u}{1+u},\qquad P_{\mathrm{mat}}(E{=}4)=\frac{p}{1+u},\qquad\langle E\rangle^{(2)}_{\mathrm{mat}}=\frac4{1+u}\in(2,4],\qquad w_{\mathrm{mat}}^{(2)}=\frac1{1+u}\in\Bigl(\tfrac12,\ 1\Bigr]\ }$$
$$\operatorname{Var}^{(2)}_{\mathrm{mat}}(E)=\frac{8p(1-p)}{(2-p)^2};\qquad\frac{\operatorname{Var}^{(2)}}{\langle E\rangle^{(2)2}}=\frac{p(1-p)}2\le\frac18,\qquad\frac{\sigma^{(2)}}{\langle E\rangle^{(2)}}\le\frac1{2\sqrt2}<\frac12\qquad[\text{machine: exact rational functions};\ \tfrac18-\tfrac{p(1-p)}2=\tfrac{(2p-1)^2}{8}\ge0];$$

### BM.141 — The Jensen residue: the exact closed form, its range, its zero locus, the two-chain companion, and the width adjudication

**Thm.**
$$(1)\quad\textbf{the residue computed:}\qquad J_3(p)\ :=\ \langle E\rangle_{\mathrm{mat}}\bigl\langle E^{-1}\bigr\rangle_{\mathrm{mat}}-1\ =\ \frac{18-27p+11p^2}{2D^2}-1,\qquad D=3-3p+p^2,\qquad p=1-4\varepsilon_q\qquad[\mathrm{BM.94}(6),(8)\ \text{re-cited}];$$
$$\boxed{\ J_3(p)\ =\ \frac{p\,(1-p)\,\bigl(9-10p+2p^2\bigr)}{2D^2}\ }\qquad[\text{machine: the polynomial identity}\ 18-27p+11p^2-2D^2=p(1-p)(9-10p+2p^2)\ \text{exact in}\ \mathbb Q[p]];$$
$$(2)\quad\textbf{the sign, the zeros, and the range:}\qquad J_3\ge0\ \ \text{on}\ p\in(0,1]\qquad[\mathrm{BM.94}(8)\text{'s Cauchy--Schwarz row re-derived};\ \text{machine:}\ 9-10p+2p^2>0\ \text{on}\ (0,1]\ \text{— its roots}\ \frac{5\pm\sqrt7}2\ \text{both exceed}\ 1\ \text{in}\ \mathbb Q(\sqrt7):\ \frac{5-\sqrt7}2>1\iff3>\sqrt7\iff9>7];$$
$$\boxed{\ J_3=0\iff p=1\iff\varepsilon_q=0\ }\qquad[\text{machine: the factor census}];\qquad J_3\bigl(\tfrac12\bigr)=\frac9{49}\qquad[\mathrm{BM.94}(8):\ \tfrac{58}{49}-1;\ \text{machine}];$$
$$J_3<\frac15\ \ \text{on}\ (0,1)\qquad[12p^4-72p^3+125p^2-81p+18>0;\ \mathrm{BM.94}(8)\ \text{re-derived};\ \text{machine: exact rational bisection, no roots on}\ (0,1)];$$
$$\boxed{\ \sup_{(0,1)}J_3=J_3(p_\ast)\in\Bigl(\frac{93}{500},\ \frac3{16}\Bigr),\qquad p_\ast\in\Bigl(\frac{288131}{524288},\ \frac{576263}{1048576}\Bigr)\ }\qquad[\text{machine: the unique critical point by Sturm isolation of}\ -44p^5+294p^4-792p^3+1062p^2-684p+162;\qquad J_3<\tfrac3{16}\ \text{strict:}\ 38p^4-228p^3+394p^2-252p+54>0\ \text{on}\ (0,1),\ \text{no roots}];$$
$$(3)\quad\textbf{the two-chain companion:}\qquad\langle E\rangle^{(2)}_{\mathrm{mat}}=\frac4{1+u},\qquad\bigl\langle E^{-1}\bigr\rangle^{(2)}_{\mathrm{mat}}=\frac{3u+1}{4(1+u)}\qquad[\mathrm{BM.137}(2);\ \text{machine}];$$
$$\boxed{\ J_2(p)\ =\ \frac{4-3p}{(2-p)^2}-1\ =\ \frac{p(1-p)}{(2-p)^2}\ =\ \frac{u(1-u)}{(1+u)^2}\ }\qquad[\text{machine: the identity exact in}\ \mathbb Q[p]];$$

$$J_2\bigl(\tfrac12\bigr)=\frac19<\frac9{49}=J_3\bigl(\tfrac12\bigr);\qquad\frac18<\frac15;\qquad\textbf{the two-chain residue is strictly tighter than the three-chain bar}\qquad[\text{machine}];$$
$$(4)\quad\textbf{the exact crossing of the two residues:}\qquad J_3-J_2=\frac{p\,(p-1)\,\bigl(6p^3-27p^2+40p-18\bigr)}{2D^2(2-p)^2}\qquad[\text{machine: the factorization exact in}\ \mathbb Q[p]];$$

**Phys.** The era's books are cleaned before they are shelved. One residue closes as void: the interior multipole content was never a missing object — the trace-only law, the absent interior density, the positionless end signs and the envelope discipline together make the internal charge resolution of a sealed composite unknowable by theorem, and coarse graining is exactly what bounds the flux. Two residues turn out to be phantom gaps: the loop realization and the connector winding are registration data of the same species as the edge phases, determined at crystallization, with every physical law — spin, parity, angular momentum from the metric, the defect ladder — derived uniformly over all realizations. Three items move to the calibration register with their values unissued and their parameter count unchanged, and the pair-correlation residue is reclassified after a uniformity census shows no clause of the era ever needed it. The final table balances every residue the era named against a disposition, and the atomic era's shopping list is written: six supply rows it receives and ten demand rows it must build, the binding channel first.

**Phys.** The continuum limit stops being a slogan and becomes a function. It takes two ledger variables — the cell's content and its chart span — and returns five exact closed forms: the linearized metric, the lapse, the materialization threshold, the flicker density, and the width. Its domain is four derived conditions, and the third of them is a capacity: a cell of content $E$ is chart-readable out to radius $r$ exactly when $E\le 2r/\mathfrak h$. The limit $\mathfrak h\to0$ is the statement that this capacity outruns every finite content, while the cell's real-edge count grows without bound — the two halves of the continuum condition, both witnessed inside the ledger. The function carries no aspect label: force identity lives in the source, the mask and the coupling profile, never in the limit itself.

### BM.147 — The metric–energy–continuum map: the dictionary bijection, the closed form of the source read, and the target

**Thm.**
$$(1)\quad\textbf{the metric is a map (the dictionary):}\qquad\bigl(a_{00},\ q_{ij},\ w_i\bigr)\in\mathcal E_{++}\oplus\mathcal E_{+-}\ \longmapsto\ g_{\mu\nu}=\Omega^2\bar g_{\mu\nu},\qquad\Omega=e^{\alpha_\Omega a_{00}},\qquad\bar g=\begin{pmatrix}-1&\varkappa N_j\\ \varkappa N_i&\delta_{ij}+\varkappa q_{ij}\end{pmatrix},\qquad N_i=\beta w_i\cdot\Omega^2\ [\mathrm{CT1.12};\ \mathrm{BM.34}(1)];$$
$$7+3=10=\tfrac{4\cdot5}2:\qquad\boxed{\ \text{the dictionary is a bijection between the ten sector coefficients and the ten metric components}\ }\qquad[\mathrm{CT1.12};\ \text{machine: the dimension count}];$$
$$\operatorname{sig}(g)=(-,+,+,+)\iff\varkappa\|q\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1\ \ \text{on the perturbative regime}\qquad[\mathrm{CT1.12}];\qquad(a_{00},q,w)=0\longmapsto\text{the flat metric}\qquad[\mathrm{BM.34}(2)];$$

**Phys.** The capstone lands. The force operator acts over the graph through eight derived steps, and its continuum limit is one function of two ledger variables with four exact domain conditions and five closed forms. The metric is the dictionary, the energy determines it through a pure-trace linearized solve, the continuum is the quotient target, and the map's capacity is exact: two $r$ over $\mathfrak h$. Past capacity nothing is lost — the ledger retains what the chart cannot read, behind a one-way membrane with maximal locked entropy. The limit is universal because the operator, the arena and the action are one, and force identity lives in three derived fingerprints and nowhere else. And the two conditions that the corpus had carried as its only extra-axiomatic imports fall out of its own structure: the ladder witnesses the richness, the spectral bound witnesses the regularity. The list is empty. The axiom surface is the entire non-derived surface. Era 1 — the foundational corpus of four eras — is closed, its ledger balanced, its books shelved, and the atomic era's requirement list written.
